title: Ukrainian (Illustrations of the IPA). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 47(3), 2017, 349–357
author: Bernd Pompino-Marschall, Elena Steriopolo, Marzena Żygis
publisher: International Phonetic Association / Cambridge University Press (open-access copy on edoc-Server, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin)
usedFor: Peer-reviewed phonetic description used for the alphabet and pronunciation pages: the six vowels written а, о, у, е, и, і, with и further back and lower than і; vowel length not contrastive; unstressed vowels tend to be less peripheral in fluent speech; hard/soft contrast limited to dental and alveolar consonants, other consonants only slightly softened before і; hard л velarized; в as a w-like sound at the end of a syllable; г as a voiced glottal fricative, pronounced like х before к (легкий); й as a glide at the end of a syllable; щ as ш + ч; п, т, к unaspirated and б, д, ґ fully voiced; no final devoicing (unlike Russian and most other Slavic languages); voicing assimilation only towards voiced (отже); free, contrastive and mobile stress (доро́га / дорога́, роби́ти, роблю́, ро́биш).
notes: DOI 10.1017/S0025100316000372, first published online 4 November 2016. Read as text extracted from the PDF; the IPA symbols did not survive extraction, so no IPA is reproduced on the site from this source. The description is based on one speaker from Bukovina educated in Kyiv; the authors note contradictory results in the literature on half-palatalized consonants, the vowel и and geminates. It describes Ukrainian sounds, not English comparisons.
